# TSDoc rules — xPack Logger

The rules for the TSDoc comments of `src/`, shared by the skills (the
`code-review`, `consistency-check`, `design-review`, and
`website-api-review` skills refer to this file, instead of repeating
them). The comments are the only hand-written source of the API
reference, which is generated by api-extractor and tsdoc2docusaurus, so
they must be accepted by API Extractor (no `ae-*` or `tsdoc-*`
warnings). The rules combine `.github/copilot-instructions.md` with
those of the `tsdoc2docusaurus-cli` project, which generates the pages.

## Coverage

- Every class, method, property, parameter, and return value has a TSDoc
  comment, including the `private` and `protected` members.
- Existing documentation is reviewed and improved where it is vague,
  repeats the signature, or is out of date with the change.
- Examples in the comments are valid and still match the signature.
- A setter has no TSDoc comment: the documentation of an accessor pair
  is on the getter, which describes both (api-extractor reports
  `ae-setter-with-docs` otherwise).
- The existing `// eslint-disable-next-line` comments are preserved.
- The lines are shorter than 80 characters.

## Structure

- The **brief description** is a single line, the only text before the
  first block tag (a comment that wraps the first sentence over several
  lines, or has paragraphs before the tags, is wrong).
- The full description follows the `@remarks` tag, which is the first
  block tag, directly after the brief description. A comment with no
  more to say than the brief description has no `@remarks`.
- The order of the tags is: `@remarks`, `@example`, `@param`,
  `@returns`, `@throws`, and `@deprecated`; the `@param` tags come
  before `@returns`, and the `@throws` tags after it.
- `@remarks` explains first why the member is useful, then how to use
  it, and finally the additional notes and details. The notes of the
  version history ("added in", "deprecated in") are bullets at the end.
- `@throws {@link ExceptionName}` is preceded by an empty line, and its
  description is on the next line. For the built-in exceptions
  (`TypeError`, `RangeError`), which `{@link}` cannot resolve
  (`ae-unresolved-link`), write the plain name, `@throws TypeError`. The exceptions thrown by assertions
  are not documented.
- Modifier tags, if any (for example `@override` or `@readonly`), come
  last.
- No `@category` tag: it is a typedoc tag; the project no longer uses
  typedoc, and the API reference is generated with api-extractor, which
  does not support it (it causes `tsdoc-undefined-tag` warnings). Do not
  add it, and report it where it is found.
- No `@public` or `@internal` tags (the release tags are not used, so
  the api-extractor messages `ae-incompatible-release-tags` and
  `ae-internal-missing-underscore` must not appear either).
- `tests/tap/160-package.ts` checks the structure of the comments of
  `src/lib/logger.ts` and that `@category` is not used; it must be kept
  in line with these rules.

## Markup

- Lists in `@remarks` use the HTML tags `<ol>` and `<li>` (ordered) or
  `<ul>` and `<li>` (unordered), not Markdown lists.
- Inside the HTML lists, use `<b>`, `<i>`, and `<code>`, not the
  Markdown syntax, and `<code>` instead of `{@link name}`. A backslash
  is not accepted by TSDoc there (`tsdoc-unnecessary-backslash`); write
  `&#92;` for it.
- Bold and italics use `<b>` and `<i>` everywhere, and tables use the
  HTML `<table>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`, `<tr>`, `<th>`, and `<td>` tags
  (no Markdown `**` or pipe tables); inside the tags, code uses `<code>`.
- Outside the HTML lists and tables, use the Markdown syntax for code
  (backticks) and `{@link name}` for links; fenced code blocks stay.

## Language

- British English spelling ("behaviour", "initialise"), a formal and
  professional tone, no contractions, the Oxford comma, and "folder"
  rather than "directory".
- Third person briefs ("Logs", "Returns", "Checks").
